codeReview.summary: The helium-cross-platform-paths feature was already implemented by a prior worker in commit 8855a96 (helium-keychain-verification feature). This worker (a43b1985) correctly identified that the implementation was already complete and verified it passes all tests. The actual code changes were: (1) linuxPath: '.config/helium' and winPath: 'AppData/Local/Helium/User Data' added to the Helium browser definition in browsers.ts, (2) helium: ['chrome'] mapping already exists in chrome-cookies.ts for Linux secret-tool lookup. Both paths follow the Chromium-based pattern as expected. The browserUserDataDir() function correctly returns non-undefined on all platforms since all three OS paths (macPath, linuxPath, winPath) are defined for Helium.

issues.description: No dedicated test for browserUserDataDir('helium') returning non-undefined on Linux or Windows. The existing test only checks on macOS (with `if (platform() === 'darwin')` guard). However, the test 'helium has linuxPath and winPath defined' verifies the browser definition has these paths, which is the core of VAL-HELIUM-005. The browserUserDataDir function is straightforward (platform + path property), so the missing platform-specific integration test is low risk.
issues.suggestion: Consider adding a unit test that mocks platform() to return 'linux' and 'win32' and verifies browserUserDataDir returns the correct path. This would make the cross-platform behavior explicit rather than inferred.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Feature overlap between helium-keychain-verification and helium-cross-platform-paths. The prior worker (8855a96) implemented both the keychain entries AND the cross-platform paths, despite the feature descriptions being separate. This is fine functionally but means the cross-platform-paths worker found nothing to do. The features.json could benefit from clearer preconditions noting that path additions may already be done by earlier features.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: Commit 8855a96 added linuxPath and winPath as part of the keychain-verification feature (noted in commit message: 'Also adds linuxPath and winPath for Helium'). Worker a43b1985 for helium-cross-platform-paths found the feature already implemented.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Linux secret-tool mapping for Chromium-based browsers: browsers that are Chromium forks without their own Linux keyring entry should map to ['chrome'] in the appNames record in chrome-cookies.ts. This pattern is used by helium, comet, and could apply to future Chromium-based browsers. This convention is not documented in AGENTS.md or the library.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: chrome-cookies.ts lines 44-50: appNames mapping. helium: ['chrome'] and comet: ['chrome'] both follow this pattern. brave has its own entry ['brave']. Only chrome, chromium, and brave have their own keyring entries on Linux.

summary: Feature PASS. Helium cross-platform paths (linuxPath and winPath) are correctly implemented in browsers.ts, following the Chromium pattern. The Linux secret-tool mapping in chrome-cookies.ts correctly maps Helium to Chrome's keyring entry. Tests verify the paths are defined. The worker correctly identified that the implementation was already complete from the prior helium-keychain-verification feature (commit 8855a96) and verified all tests pass. One non-blocking observation: no platform-specific integration test for browserUserDataDir on Linux/Windows, though the browser definition test covers the core requirement of VAL-HELIUM-005.
